intro: Welcome back! At B1 you wrote a short review with a recommendation. Now you'll write like a real reviewer and blogger: reviews of a series, an app or a café that judge fairly and say exactly who should try them, and articles with a title and a first line that make people want to read on. Warm-up: think of the last series you couldn't stop watching, or an app you can't live without.
teachingNotes: This writing lesson builds on b1-writing-stories-articles: a title and a hook, one main idea per paragraph with a topic sentence first, the good and the bad (However, … / although), an opinion with reasons, and a recommendation with I'd recommend + -ing / a noun and It's worth + -ing. Recap it in one line, don't re-teach it. New at B2: the four-part review, evaluative language, balanced criticism, recommendation patterns with who it's for, and engaging article titles, openings and tone. Grammar limits: A0–B1 grammar only. No despite / in spite of (not taught yet: use although or However,), no non-defining relative clauses (', which …'), participle clauses, third conditional, wish or past modals in examples. Treat I'd recommend that you + base verb, It's well worth a try, give it a miss and live up to / fall short of as phrases to remember.

A B2 review (about 140–190 words, like the Cambridge B2 First exam) helps the reader decide. Four parts: 1) a hook (a strong opinion, a surprise, a question); 2) a short description WITHOUT spoilers (what it is, who it's about or what it does), with the story told in the present simple (The series follows Dewi …), a tendency of English reviews; 3) strengths and weaknesses, each with a specific example (which scene, which feature, which price), not just 'good' or 'nice'; 4) a recommendation and who it's for (I'd highly recommend it to anyone who …; it's not for you if …). Common errors: retelling the whole plot, including the ending; telling the plot in the past; general words with no example; a review that is 100% positive or 100% negative; no clear verdict at the end.

Evaluative language, in groups. Stories (films, series, books): gripping (so exciting you can't stop), well-paced, predictable, convincing acting, stunning (visuals). Products and apps: user-friendly, reliable, glitchy, good value for money, overpriced. Verdicts: live up to the hype / expectations (be as good as people say), fall short of expectations (not be as good), a must-see. Indonesian traps: 'harganya overprice' → overpriced, with -d (*'The drinks are overprice'); 'worth it banget' → It's really / well worth it (*'It's very worth'); *'lives up the hype' (missing to); B1 recap: *'very recommended' → I'd really recommend it. Collocation tendency: gripping goes with stories, user-friendly with apps and machines (*'a gripping app' sounds odd).

Balanced criticism and recommendations. Although + the weakness, then the strength in the main part when the overall opinion is positive (Although the plot is predictable, the acting is superb); swap them and the overall opinion sounds negative. This is a tendency about emphasis, so only test clear cases where the overall opinion is given. Other ways in: It isn't perfect, though. / My only complaint is (that) … / The only downside is …. The node's common error: *'I recommend you to watch it', from 'merekomendasikan kamu untuk' → I recommend watching it / I'd recommend that you watch it / I'd recommend it to you. Also *'I'd recommend to watch it'. Accept 'I'd recommend you watch it' (informal, that dropped). 'I'd recommend you watching it' is non-standard: give partial credit. Negative recommendations: I wouldn't recommend it; Give it a miss (British, informal).

Articles (blog, office newsletter, campus magazine) share ideas and experiences about a topic; nobody has to read them, so the title and first two lines matter most. Titles: a question (Is the New MRT Line Worth the Wait?), a number (5 Reasons to Leave Your Car at Home), a pun (On the Right Track: track = the railway line + 'going the right way'); puns are optional and a clear question or number title is always fine. Openings: a question to the reader, a surprising fact or number, a short anecdote (a very short true story from the writer's life). Address the reader: you, Have you ever …?, Imagine …. Tone: lively but not chatty. Indonesian traps at both ends: social-media style (*'Hello guys! Welcome back to my blog hehe', OMG, sooo, gonna, emoji, '!!!', 'Thank you for reading') and school-essay style (*'In this article, I will discuss …', *'Nowadays, transportation is very important in our life', from 'Di era globalisasi ini …' / 'Dewasa ini …'). End with a question, a tip or a challenge for the reader.

Feedback: for the free reviews and articles (140–190 words), praise the shape first, then correct one or two things only, usually the recommend pattern, a spoiler, a vague word or an over-chatty / over-formal opening. British vs American: film / movie, series (one season, BrE) / season, favourite / favorite, 7.30 / 7:30. Contexts: Indonesian Netflix series, e-wallet apps, cafés in Bandung, the MRT and KRL in Jakarta; rupiah prices. The series, app and café names in examples (Jakarta After Dark, Rumah Pak Hasan, DompetKita, SakuPay, Kopi Awan) are made up. Typed answers are lowercased when checked, so give feedback on capitals and title case in the free writing, not in the checkpoint.

keyPoints.title: A review that helps the reader decide
keyPoints.explanation: Write four parts: a hook; a short description without spoilers (tell the story in the present simple: The series follows …); strengths and weaknesses, each with a specific example and evaluative words (gripping, user-friendly, overpriced, lives up to the hype); and a recommendation that says who it's for. Be fair: Although + the weakness, then your main opinion. Recommend + -ing or that you + verb, never 'recommend you to'.

examples.en: Once it gets going, the series is gripping and well-paced.
examples.id: Begitu ceritanya mulai jalan, serialnya seru sekali dan temponya pas.

examples.en: Although the app is a little slow at first, it's reliable and easy to use.
examples.id: Meskipun aplikasinya agak lambat di awal, aplikasinya andal dan mudah dipakai.

examples.en: I'd highly recommend it to anyone who loves crime dramas.
examples.id: Aku sangat merekomendasikannya untuk siapa saja yang suka drama kriminal.

id.title: Review yang membantu pembaca memutuskan
id.explanation: Tulis empat bagian: kalimat pengait (hook); deskripsi singkat tanpa spoiler (ceritakan alurnya dengan present simple: The series follows …); kelebihan dan kekurangan, masing-masing dengan contoh yang spesifik dan kata penilaian (gripping, user-friendly, overpriced, lives up to the hype); dan rekomendasi yang menyebut cocok untuk siapa. Bersikaplah adil: Although + kekurangannya, lalu pendapat utamamu. Recommend + -ing atau that you + kata kerja, jangan pernah 'recommend you to'.

keyPoints.title: An article that pulls the reader in
keyPoints.explanation: Nobody has to read an article, so the title and the first two lines must make them want to. Title: a question, a number or a pun. Opening: a question to the reader, a surprising fact, or a short anecdote (a true mini-story from your life). Then talk to the reader (you, Have you ever …?) in a lively but not chatty tone: no 'Hello guys!', and no 'In this article, I will discuss …'.

examples.en: 5 Reasons to Leave Your Car at Home
examples.id: 5 Alasan untuk Meninggalkan Mobilmu di Rumah

examples.en: Last month, I spent 46 hours in my car. Not on a road trip to Bali: just driving to work and back.
examples.id: Bulan lalu, aku menghabiskan 46 jam di mobil. Bukan untuk road trip ke Bali: cuma menyetir ke kantor dan pulang.

examples.en: If you live in Jakarta, you probably know the feeling.
examples.id: Kalau kamu tinggal di Jakarta, kamu mungkin tahu rasanya.

id.title: Artikel yang menarik pembaca
id.explanation: Tidak ada yang wajib membaca artikel, jadi judul dan dua baris pertamanya harus membuat orang ingin membaca. Judul: pertanyaan, angka, atau permainan kata (pun). Pembuka: pertanyaan untuk pembaca, fakta yang mengejutkan, atau anekdot singkat (cerita mini yang benar-benar terjadi dalam hidupmu). Lalu ajak pembaca bicara (you, Have you ever …?) dengan nada yang hidup tapi tidak terlalu santai: jangan 'Hello guys!', dan jangan 'In this article, I will discuss …'.

Checklist: a title and a hook; a short description in the present simple, with no spoilers; two strengths and one weakness, each with a specific example; at least two evaluative words (gripping, well-paced, user-friendly, overpriced, lives up to the hype …); fair criticism (Although … / My only complaint is …); a clear recommendation and who it's for.

i would highly recommend it to anyone who
id recommend

Checklist: an engaging title (a question, a number or a pun); an opening with a question, a surprising fact or a short anecdote; talk to the reader (you, Have you ever …?); 2–3 paragraphs, each with a topic sentence; a lively but not chatty tone (no 'Hello guys', no 'In this article, I will discuss'); an ending with a question, a tip or a challenge for the reader.

assessment.prompt: The last line of Budi's review of an e-wallet app has a common mistake. Rewrite it correctly, starting with I'd recommend: I recommend you to try SakuPay.
acceptableAnswers: id recommend that you try sakupay
i would recommend that you try sakupay
i would recommend you try sakupay
i would recommend sakupay to you
i would highly recommend trying sakupay
id recommend giving sakupay a try
i would recommend giving sakupay a try
assessment.rubric: Correct: I'd recommend trying SakuPay / I'd recommend that you try SakuPay; also I'd recommend you try SakuPay (informal, 'that' dropped) and I'd recommend SakuPay (to you). 'I'd recommend you trying SakuPay' = 40 (non-standard). 'I'd recommend to try SakuPay' = 20 (recommend isn't followed by to + verb). Keeping 'you to try' = 0 (the mistake the item asks to fix).

assessment.prompt: Complete Sari's review of a Netflix series with ONE adjective that means 'so exciting that you can't stop watching': I started episode 1 at nine in the evening and only stopped at three in the morning. The story is absolutely ___ .
assessment.rubric: Correct: gripping (also addictive, compelling, riveting, thrilling, binge-worthy). 'exciting' = 50 (right idea, but 'absolutely exciting' sounds unnatural and it doesn't say you can't stop). 'gripped' = 50 (that's how the viewer feels: I was gripped). 'unmissable' = 60 (a must-see, but not quite 'can't stop watching'). 'amazing', 'brilliant', 'great' = 40 (positive, but general, not the meaning asked). 'boring', 'predictable', 'well-paced' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Rina's overall opinion of a café in Bandung is positive. Join her two sentences into one sentence that starts with Although: The café is overpriced. The view of the city is stunning.
acceptableAnswers: although the cafe is overpriced the view of the city is stunning
although the cafe is a bit overpriced the view of the city is stunning
although the cafe is a little overpriced the view of the city is stunning
although its overpriced the view of the city is stunning
although it is overpriced the view of the city is stunning
although the cafe is overpriced its view of the city is stunning
although the cafe is overpriced the city view is stunning
assessment.rubric: Correct: Although the café is overpriced, the view of the city is stunning (the weakness after Although, the main, positive opinion in the other part). 'Although the view of the city is stunning, the café is overpriced' = 40 (correct grammar, but now the overall opinion sounds negative). 'Although …, but …' = 30 (one linker per sentence). A missing verb ('Although the café overpriced') = 50.

assessment.prompt: Pak Hasan is writing an article for his office newsletter about paying for everything with an e-wallet for a whole week. Which title will make the most people want to read it? Write A, B or C. A: E-Wallets B: Can You Survive a Week Without Cash? C: The Advantages and Disadvantages of Digital Payment Systems
assessment.rubric: Correct: B (a question title that talks to the reader and makes them curious). A = 0 (one word, it gives no reason to read on). C = 0 (a dry essay or report title, not an engaging article title).

assessment.prompt: Dimas is writing an article for his campus magazine about the best cafés in Bandung for studying. Which opening is the best? Write A, B or C. A: Hello guys!! Welcome back to my article hehe. Today I want to share about cafés for studying. B: In this article, I will discuss the advantages and disadvantages of studying in cafés in Bandung. C: Have you ever tried to finish an assignment in a café where the Wi-Fi died every ten minutes?
assessment.rubric: Correct: C (a question to the reader about a real experience: lively, but not chatty). A = 0 (too chatty: a social-media greeting, '!!', 'hehe', and 'share about' is not English). B = 0 (too stiff: a school-essay opening that tells the reader nothing interesting).

assessment.prompt: A blog article has this title: A Latte to Love: Bandung's Best Study Cafés. One word in the title is a pun (a word that plays with two meanings or two sounds). Write that word.
assessment.rubric: Correct: latte (it's a coffee, and 'a latte' sounds like 'a lot': there's a lot to love in Bandung's cafés). 'love', 'best', 'cafés' or 'study' = 0 (they have only their normal meaning here).

material.title: A review that helps the reader decide

blocks.text:
Quick recap from B1: a title, a hook, one main idea per paragraph with a topic sentence first, the good and the bad, and a recommendation (*I'd recommend + -ing*, *It's worth + -ing*).
At B2, a review is longer (about **140–190 words**, like the Cambridge B2 First exam) and has one clear job: help the reader **decide** if a film, series, product, app or place is right for **them**. Use four parts:
- **1. A hook**: a first line that makes people curious: a strong opinion, a surprise, a question.
- **2. A short description, without spoilers**: what it is, who it's about or what it does. A **spoiler** (bocoran cerita) gives away a surprise or the ending. Tell the story in the **present simple**: *The series **follows** Dewi …*, not *followed*. That's a habit of English reviews: the story 'happens' every time someone watches it.
- **3. Strengths and weaknesses, with specific examples**: not just *The acting is good*, but which actor, which scene, what exactly.
- **4. A recommendation and who it's for**: who will love it, and who should skip it.

id.text:
Ulasan singkat dari B1: judul, kalimat pengait (hook), satu ide pokok per paragraf dengan topic sentence di depan, sisi baik dan buruknya, dan rekomendasi (*I'd recommend + -ing*, *It's worth + -ing*).
Di B2, review lebih panjang (sekitar **140–190 kata**, seperti ujian Cambridge B2 First) dan punya satu tugas yang jelas: membantu pembaca **memutuskan** apakah sebuah film, serial, produk, aplikasi atau tempat cocok untuk **mereka**. Pakai empat bagian:
- **1. Hook**: kalimat pertama yang membuat penasaran: pendapat yang kuat, kejutan, atau pertanyaan.
- **2. Deskripsi singkat, tanpa spoiler**: apa itu, tentang siapa, atau apa fungsinya. **Spoiler** (bocoran cerita) membocorkan kejutan atau akhir cerita. Ceritakan alurnya dengan **present simple**: *The series **follows** Dewi …*, bukan *followed*. Ini kebiasaan review dalam bahasa Inggris: ceritanya 'terjadi' lagi setiap kali ada yang menonton.
- **3. Kelebihan dan kekurangan, dengan contoh spesifik**: bukan cuma *The acting is good*, tapi aktor yang mana, adegan yang mana, apa tepatnya.
- **4. Rekomendasi dan cocok untuk siapa**: siapa yang akan menyukainya, dan siapa yang sebaiknya melewatkannya.

rows.en: Jakarta After Dark: give it two episodes. I almost gave up on this series after twenty minutes. I'm very glad I didn't.
rows.id: Jakarta After Dark: beri dia dua episode. Aku hampir berhenti menonton serial ini setelah dua puluh menit. Untung aku tidak berhenti.

rows.en: Jakarta After Dark is a new eight-episode Indonesian crime series on Netflix. It follows Dewi, a young journalist who starts looking into a string of robberies in the city's old markets. Soon, her story becomes dangerous, for her and for her family.
rows.id: Jakarta After Dark adalah serial kriminal Indonesia baru di Netflix, delapan episode. Ceritanya tentang Dewi, jurnalis muda yang mulai menyelidiki serangkaian perampokan di pasar-pasar tua kota itu. Tak lama kemudian, liputannya menjadi berbahaya, untuk dirinya dan keluarganya.

rows.en: Once it gets going, the series is gripping and well-paced. Almost every episode ends with a question that makes you press 'Next episode' straight away. The acting is convincing too: Dewi is nervous but clever, and you believe her completely. And the night scenes of Glodok and Kota Tua look stunning.
rows.id: Begitu ceritanya mulai jalan, serialnya seru sekali dan temponya pas. Hampir setiap episode berakhir dengan pertanyaan yang membuatmu langsung menekan 'Next episode'. Aktingnya juga meyakinkan: Dewi gugup tapi cerdas, dan kamu benar-benar percaya padanya. Dan adegan malam di Glodok dan Kota Tua tampak memukau.

rows.en: It isn't perfect, though. The first episode is slow and has too many characters, and a storyline about Dewi's brother is a little predictable. My only real complaint is the music: it's far too loud in the action scenes.
rows.id: Tapi serial ini tidak sempurna. Episode pertamanya lambat dan tokohnya terlalu banyak, dan satu alur cerita tentang adik Dewi agak mudah ditebak. Satu-satunya keluhanku yang serius adalah musiknya: terlalu keras di adegan laga.

rows.en: Overall, it lives up to the hype. I'd highly recommend it to anyone who loves crime dramas, but it's not for you if you want non-stop action. Just give it two episodes before you decide.
rows.id: Secara keseluruhan, serial ini memang sebagus yang diheboh-hebohkan. Aku sangat merekomendasikannya untuk siapa saja yang suka drama kriminal, tapi ini bukan untukmu kalau kamu mau aksi tanpa henti. Beri saja dua episode sebelum kamu memutuskan.

blocks.text:
**No spoilers, please.** In the description, say what the story is **about**, not how it **ends**: *In the last episode, Dewi finds out that …* ✗. If you really must mention something from later in the story, warn the reader first: *(Small spoiler!)*.
**British vs American:** a *film* (British) = a *movie* (American). In British English, a *series* can also mean one **season** of a show: *series 2* (British) = *season 2* (American).

id.text:
**Jangan spoiler.** Di deskripsi, ceritakan ceritanya **tentang apa**, bukan **bagaimana akhirnya**: *In the last episode, Dewi finds out that …* ✗. Kalau kamu benar-benar perlu menyebut sesuatu dari bagian akhir cerita, peringatkan pembaca dulu: *(Small spoiler!)*.
**British vs American:** *film* (Inggris) = *movie* (Amerika). Dalam bahasa Inggris British, *series* juga bisa berarti satu **musim** sebuah acara: *series 2* (British) = *season 2* (Amerika).

blocks.prompt: Which sentence is the best hook for a review of an e-wallet app called DompetKita?
options: This is my review of the DompetKita app.
I deleted three payment apps last month. DompetKita is the one I kept.
DompetKita is an app for paying.
blocks.explain: A hook makes the reader curious: why did the writer delete three apps, and why keep this one? 'This is my review of …' and 'DompetKita is an app for paying' are true, but they give no reason to read on.

id.prompt: Kalimat mana yang paling bagus sebagai hook untuk review aplikasi dompet digital bernama DompetKita?
id.explain: Hook membuat pembaca penasaran: kenapa penulisnya menghapus tiga aplikasi, dan kenapa menyimpan yang ini? 'This is my review of …' dan 'DompetKita is an app for paying' memang benar, tapi tidak memberi alasan untuk terus membaca.

material.title: Words that judge: gripping, user-friendly, overpriced

blocks.text:
At B2, swap general words (*good, nice, bad, interesting*) for **evaluative words**: words that give your judgement (penilaian) **and** say something specific. Learn them in groups, because they go with different things:
- **Stories** (films, series, books): *gripping, well-paced, predictable, convincing* (acting), *stunning* (to look at).
- **Products and apps**: *user-friendly, reliable, glitchy, good value for money, overpriced*.
- **The final verdict**: *live up to the hype* = be as good as everyone says (*the hype* = the huge excitement online and in the media, 'heboh'-nya); *fall short of expectations* = not be as good as people hoped. Both need a noun after them: *live up **to** the hype / its name*, *fall short **of** expectations*.
Then **prove** your word with one detail: *The app is user-friendly: my mother learned it in five minutes.*

id.text:
Di B2, ganti kata-kata umum (*good, nice, bad, interesting*) dengan **kata penilaian** (evaluative words): kata yang memberi penilaianmu **dan** mengatakan sesuatu yang spesifik. Pelajari per kelompok, karena pasangannya berbeda:
- **Cerita** (film, serial, buku): *gripping* (seru sekali), *well-paced* (temponya pas), *predictable* (mudah ditebak), *convincing* (akting yang meyakinkan), *stunning* (memukau dilihat).
- **Produk dan aplikasi**: *user-friendly* (mudah dipakai), *reliable* (andal), *glitchy* (sering error), *good value for money* (sepadan dengan harganya), *overpriced* (kemahalan).
- **Kesimpulan akhir**: *live up to the hype* = memang sebagus yang dikatakan semua orang (*the hype* = kehebohan besar di internet dan media); *fall short of expectations* = tidak sebagus yang diharapkan. Keduanya butuh kata benda sesudahnya: *live up **to** the hype / its name*, *fall short **of** expectations*.
Lalu **buktikan** kata itu dengan satu detail: *The app is user-friendly: my mother learned it in five minutes.*

blocks.text:
**Indonesian–English traps:**
- *Harganya overprice* → the English adjective ends in **-d**, like *crowded*: *The drinks are **overpriced*** ✓, *The drinks are overprice* ✗.
- *Worth it banget* → *It's **really** worth it* / *It's **well** worth it* ✓, not *It's very worth* ✗.
- Don't drop the little word: *lives up the hype* ✗ → *lives up **to** the hype* ✓.
- Match the word to the thing: a series can be *gripping*, an app can be *user-friendly*, but *a gripping app* sounds strange.
- **One specific example beats ten 'very good's.** *The app is very good* ✗ tells the reader nothing; *Paying for an ojek takes two taps* ✓ shows it.

id.text:
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia–Inggris:**
- *Harganya overprice* → kata sifat bahasa Inggrisnya berakhiran **-d**, seperti *crowded*: *The drinks are **overpriced*** ✓, *The drinks are overprice* ✗.
- *Worth it banget* → *It's **really** worth it* / *It's **well** worth it* ✓, bukan *It's very worth* ✗.
- Jangan hilangkan kata kecilnya: *lives up the hype* ✗ → *lives up **to** the hype* ✓.
- Cocokkan katanya dengan bendanya: serial bisa *gripping*, aplikasi bisa *user-friendly*, tapi *a gripping app* terdengar aneh.
- **Satu contoh spesifik lebih kuat dari sepuluh 'very good'.** *The app is very good* ✗ tidak memberi tahu pembaca apa-apa; *Paying for an ojek takes two taps* ✓ menunjukkannya.

blocks.prompt: A review of a phone says: 'It has a great camera and a big battery, and it costs only Rp2,500,000.' Which phrase fits best?
blocks.explain: A great camera and a big battery for a low price = **good value for money**. 'Overpriced' is the opposite (too expensive for what you get), and 'well-paced' is for stories, not phones.

id.prompt: Sebuah review ponsel mengatakan: 'It has a great camera and a big battery, and it costs only Rp2,500,000.' Frasa mana yang paling cocok?
id.explain: Kamera bagus dan baterai besar dengan harga murah = **good value for money** (sepadan dengan harganya). 'Overpriced' artinya kebalikannya (kemahalan), dan 'well-paced' dipakai untuk cerita, bukan ponsel.

material.title: Fair criticism and a clear recommendation

blocks.text:
A good reviewer is **fair**: even in a positive review, name a weakness; even in a negative one, name something good. Readers trust a balanced review.
Use **although** (from B1) with the weakness in one part and the strength in the other. The part **without** although is what the reader remembers, so put your **main** opinion there (a strong tendency, not a strict rule):
- *Although the plot is predictable, the acting is superb.* → overall: positive.
- *Although the acting is superb, the plot is predictable.* → overall: negative.
Other ways to add a weakness: *It isn't perfect, though.* / *My only complaint is (that) …* / *The only downside is …*
Then end with a **clear recommendation and who it's for**:
- *I'd recommend **watching** it / **downloading** it.* (recommend + -ing)
- *I'd recommend **that you watch** it.* (that + you + the base verb, the form in the dictionary; in informal writing *that* can disappear: *I'd recommend you watch it*)
- *I'd **highly** recommend it **to** anyone who loves crime dramas / **to** students on a budget.*
- *It's **well worth a try** / a visit / the money.* (*well* = really, here)
- *If you're a fan of …, you'll love it.* / *It's not for you if …*
- Not a fan? *I wouldn't recommend it.* / *Give it a miss.* (British, informal: skip it)
*I'd recommend that you …*, *It's well worth a try* and *Give it a miss* are **phrases to remember**: learn them as they are.

id.text:
Reviewer yang baik itu **adil**: bahkan di review yang positif, sebutkan satu kekurangan; bahkan di review yang negatif, sebutkan sesuatu yang bagus. Pembaca lebih percaya pada review yang seimbang.
Pakai **although** (dari B1) dengan kekurangan di satu bagian dan kelebihan di bagian lainnya. Bagian yang **tanpa** although adalah yang diingat pembaca, jadi taruh pendapat **utamamu** di sana (kecenderungan yang kuat, bukan aturan mati):
- *Although the plot is predictable, the acting is superb.* (superb = luar biasa bagus) → kesimpulannya: positif.
- *Although the acting is superb, the plot is predictable.* → kesimpulannya: negatif.
Cara lain menambahkan kekurangan: *It isn't perfect, though.* (Tapi tidak sempurna.) / *My only complaint is (that) …* (Satu-satunya keluhanku adalah …) / *The only downside is …* (Satu-satunya kekurangannya adalah …)
Lalu tutup dengan **rekomendasi yang jelas dan cocok untuk siapa**:
- *I'd recommend **watching** it / **downloading** it.* (recommend + -ing)
- *I'd recommend **that you watch** it.* (that + you + kata kerja bentuk dasar, bentuk yang ada di kamus; dalam tulisan santai *that* boleh hilang: *I'd recommend you watch it*)
- *I'd **highly** recommend it **to** anyone who loves crime dramas / **to** students on a budget.* (sangat aku rekomendasikan untuk …)
- *It's **well worth a try** / a visit / the money.* (sangat layak dicoba / dikunjungi / sepadan dengan uangnya; *well* di sini = benar-benar)
- *If you're a fan of …, you'll love it.* / *It's not for you if …*
- Tidak suka? *I wouldn't recommend it.* / *Give it a miss.* (British, santai: lewatkan saja)
*I'd recommend that you …*, *It's well worth a try* dan *Give it a miss* adalah **frasa untuk diingat**: hafalkan saja bentuknya.

rows.en: Although the app is a little slow at first, it's reliable and easy to use.
rows.id: Meskipun aplikasinya agak lambat di awal, aplikasinya andal dan mudah dipakai.
rows.note: weakness after although, main opinion last

id.note: kekurangan sesudah although, pendapat utama di akhir

rows.en: My only complaint is that the menu is only in Indonesian.
rows.id: Satu-satunya keluhanku adalah menunya hanya dalam bahasa Indonesia.

rows.en: I'd recommend downloading it before your next trip.
rows.id: Aku sarankan unduh aplikasinya sebelum perjalananmu berikutnya.

rows.id: Aku sarankan kamu datang sebelum jam sembilan supaya dapat meja dekat jendela.

id.note: recommend that you + kata kerja bentuk dasar

rows.en: I'd highly recommend it to anyone who works from cafés.
rows.id: Aku sangat merekomendasikannya untuk siapa saja yang bekerja dari kafe.

rows.en: It's well worth a try if you hate carrying cash.

blocks.text:
**The recommend trap.** In Indonesian we say *Saya merekomendasikan kamu untuk menonton …*, so many learners write *I recommend you to watch it.* ✗ In English, **recommend** isn't followed by a person + *to*. Choose:
- *I recommend **watching** it.* / *I'd recommend **watching** it.* ✓
- *I'd recommend **that you watch** it.* ✓
- *I'd recommend **it to you**.* ✓ (the thing first, then *to* + the person)
Also not *I'd recommend **to watch** it* ✗. And from B1: *It's worth to try* ✗ → *It's worth **trying*** ✓; *very recommended* ✗ → *I'd really recommend it* ✓.

id.text:
**Jebakan recommend.** Dalam bahasa Indonesia kita bilang *Saya merekomendasikan kamu untuk menonton …*, jadi banyak pelajar menulis *I recommend you to watch it.* ✗ Dalam bahasa Inggris, **recommend** tidak diikuti orang + *to*. Pilih:
- *I recommend **watching** it.* / *I'd recommend **watching** it.* ✓
- *I'd recommend **that you watch** it.* ✓
- *I'd recommend **it to you**.* ✓ (bendanya dulu, lalu *to* + orangnya)
Juga bukan *I'd recommend **to watch** it* ✗. Dan dari B1: *It's worth to try* ✗ → *It's worth **trying*** ✓; *very recommended* ✗ → *I'd really recommend it* ✓.

blocks.prompt: Rina loved the hotel overall. Which sentence shows that?
options: Although the breakfast was amazing, the rooms were small and noisy.
Although the rooms were small, the breakfast was amazing and the staff were lovely.
Although the rooms were small, but the breakfast was amazing.
blocks.explain: The weakness goes after **Although**, and the main, positive opinion goes in the other part: *the breakfast was amazing and the staff were lovely*. The first sentence sounds negative overall, and the third uses although and but together (one linker per sentence).

id.prompt: Secara keseluruhan Rina sangat suka hotelnya. Kalimat mana yang menunjukkan itu?
id.explain: Kekurangannya ditaruh sesudah **Although**, dan pendapat utama yang positif ada di bagian lainnya: *the breakfast was amazing and the staff were lovely*. Kalimat pertama terdengar negatif secara keseluruhan, dan kalimat ketiga memakai although dan but sekaligus (satu kata penghubung per kalimat).

id.title: Kritik yang adil dan rekomendasi yang jelas

material.title: Articles: a title and an opening that pull readers in

blocks.text:
An **article** (for a blog, a company newsletter, a campus magazine, a website) doesn't judge one thing like a review: it shares ideas and experiences about a **topic**, like a new MRT line or living without cash. Nobody **has** to read it, so the title and the first two lines must make people **want** to.
**Engaging titles** (judul yang menarik), three easy types:
- **A question**: *Is the New MRT Line Worth the Wait?*
- **A number**: *5 Reasons to Leave Your Car at Home*
- **A pun** (a word that plays with two meanings or two sounds): *On the Right Track*. A *track* is the railway line, and *on the right track* also means 'going the right way'. Puns are fun but optional: a clear question or number title is always fine.
In titles, the important words often start with a capital letter (*On the Right Track*), but many blogs use a capital for the first word only. Both are fine.
**Engaging openings**, the first one or two sentences:
- **A question to the reader**: *How long did your trip to work take this morning?*
- **A surprising fact** or number: *Last month, I spent 46 hours in my car.*
- **An anecdote** (a very short true story from your life): *Last Monday, I stood for an hour on a packed KRL with my face in a stranger's backpack.*
Then **talk to the reader**: use *you*, ask *Have you ever …?*, or start with *Imagine …*. It feels like a conversation.

id.text:
**Artikel** (untuk blog, buletin kantor, majalah kampus, situs web) tidak menilai satu benda seperti review: artikel berbagi ide dan pengalaman tentang suatu **topik**, misalnya jalur MRT baru atau hidup tanpa uang tunai. Tidak ada yang **wajib** membacanya, jadi judul dan dua baris pertamanya harus membuat orang **ingin** membaca.
**Judul yang menarik**, tiga jenis yang mudah:
- **Pertanyaan**: *Is the New MRT Line Worth the Wait?*
- **Angka**: *5 Reasons to Leave Your Car at Home*
- **Pun** (permainan kata: satu kata dengan dua arti atau dua bunyi): *On the Right Track*. *Track* adalah jalur rel kereta, dan *on the right track* juga berarti 'berada di jalan yang benar'. Pun itu seru tapi tidak wajib: judul berupa pertanyaan atau angka yang jelas selalu boleh.
Di judul, kata-kata penting sering diawali huruf kapital (*On the Right Track*), tapi banyak blog hanya memakai huruf kapital di kata pertama. Dua-duanya boleh.
**Pembuka yang menarik**, satu atau dua kalimat pertama:
- **Pertanyaan untuk pembaca**: *How long did your trip to work take this morning?*
- **Fakta** atau angka **yang mengejutkan**: *Last month, I spent 46 hours in my car.*
- **Anekdot** (cerita sangat pendek yang benar-benar terjadi dalam hidupmu): *Last Monday, I stood for an hour on a packed KRL with my face in a stranger's backpack.*
Lalu **ajak pembaca bicara**: pakai *you*, tanyakan *Have you ever …?*, atau mulai dengan *Imagine …*. Rasanya seperti mengobrol.

rows.en: On the Right Track: My Month Without a Car
rows.id: Di Jalur yang Benar: Sebulan Tanpa Mobil

rows.en: Last month, I spent 46 hours in my car. Not on a road trip to Bali: just driving to work and back. If you live in Jakarta, you probably know the feeling.
rows.id: Bulan lalu, aku menghabiskan 46 jam di mobil. Bukan untuk road trip ke Bali: cuma menyetir ke kantor dan pulang. Kalau kamu tinggal di Jakarta, kamu mungkin tahu rasanya.
rows.note: opening: a surprising number, then talking to the reader

id.note: pembuka: angka yang mengejutkan, lalu mengajak pembaca bicara

rows.en: So when the new MRT line opened near my house, I decided to leave the car at home for a month. The results surprised me. My trip now takes 35 minutes instead of an hour and a half, and it costs less than parking.
rows.id: Jadi waktu jalur MRT baru dibuka dekat rumahku, aku memutuskan meninggalkan mobil di rumah selama sebulan. Hasilnya mengejutkan. Perjalananku sekarang 35 menit, bukan satu setengah jam, dan biayanya lebih murah daripada parkir.

rows.en: It isn't all perfect. At 7.30 a.m. the trains are packed, and the walk from the station to my office is hot. But I read on the train, I'm never late for meetings, and I've lost two kilos from all the walking.
rows.id: Tidak semuanya sempurna. Jam 7.30 pagi keretanya penuh sesak, dan jalan kaki dari stasiun ke kantorku panas. Tapi aku bisa membaca di kereta, aku tidak pernah terlambat rapat, dan berat badanku turun dua kilo karena banyak jalan kaki.

rows.en: So, is it time to give your car a holiday? Try the MRT for one week. You might not want to go back.
rows.id: Jadi, sudah waktunya memberi mobilmu liburan? Coba naik MRT selama satu minggu. Bisa jadi kamu tidak mau kembali.
rows.note: ending: a question and a challenge for the reader

id.note: penutup: pertanyaan dan tantangan untuk pembaca

blocks.text:
**Lively, but not chatty.** A good article sounds like a smart friend talking: contractions (*it's, don't*), short and longer sentences, a question or two, a little humour. Avoid two extremes:
- **Too chatty**, like a caption or a vlog: *Hello guys! Welcome back to my blog!! Today I want to share about the MRT hehe* ✗. No greetings, *OMG*, *sooo*, *gonna*, emoji, '!!!' or *Thank you for reading*. (And *share about* isn't English: *tell you about* ✓.)
- **Too stiff**, like a school essay: *In this article, I will discuss the advantages and disadvantages of the MRT.* ✗ / *Nowadays, transportation is very important in our life.* ✗ At school we often start with *Di era globalisasi ini …* or *Dewasa ini …*; in an English article, an opening like that makes readers stop reading.
*7.30* is British; Americans write *7:30*. *humour* is British; Americans write *humor*.

id.text:
**Hidup, tapi tidak terlalu santai.** Artikel yang bagus terdengar seperti teman pintar yang sedang bicara: kontraksi (bentuk singkat seperti *it's, don't*), kalimat pendek dan agak panjang, satu-dua pertanyaan, sedikit humor. Hindari dua ujung:
- **Terlalu santai**, seperti caption atau vlog: *Hello guys! Welcome back to my blog!! Today I want to share about the MRT hehe* ✗. Jangan ada salam, *OMG*, *sooo*, *gonna*, emoji, '!!!' atau *Thank you for reading*. (Dan *share about* bukan bahasa Inggris yang benar: *tell you about* ✓.)
- **Terlalu kaku**, seperti esai sekolah: *In this article, I will discuss the advantages and disadvantages of the MRT.* ✗ / *Nowadays, transportation is very important in our life.* ✗ Di sekolah kita sering membuka dengan *Di era globalisasi ini …* atau *Dewasa ini …*; di artikel bahasa Inggris, pembuka seperti itu membuat pembaca berhenti membaca.
*7.30* itu British; orang Amerika menulis *7:30*. *humour* itu British; orang Amerika menulis *humor*.

blocks.prompt: Which title will make the most people want to read an article about saving money?
options: 7 Small Habits That Saved Me Rp1 Million a Month
The Importance of Saving Money in Modern Life
blocks.explain: A number title with a specific result (Rp1 million a month) makes readers curious: which seven habits? 'Money' is too short to say anything, and 'The Importance of …' sounds like a school essay.

id.prompt: Judul mana yang akan membuat paling banyak orang ingin membaca artikel tentang menabung?
id.explain: Judul berangka dengan hasil yang spesifik (Rp1 juta sebulan) membuat pembaca penasaran: tujuh kebiasaan apa saja? 'Money' terlalu pendek untuk mengatakan apa pun, dan 'The Importance of …' terdengar seperti esai sekolah.

id.title: Artikel: judul dan pembuka yang menarik pembaca

blocks.text:
Read your text once more before you post it.
**A review** (140–190 words):
- A title and a **hook**; a short description in the **present simple**, with **no spoilers**.
- At least two **strengths** and one **weakness**, each with a **specific example**, and evaluative words instead of *good / nice / bad*.
- **Fair**: *Although* + the weakness, then your main opinion.
- A **recommendation** and **who it's for**: *I'd recommend + -ing / that you + verb*, *I'd highly recommend it to …*, *It's well worth a try if …*. Not *recommend you to*.
**An article** (140–190 words):
- A **title** with a question, a number or a pun.
- An **opening** with a question, a surprising fact or an anecdote, and you talk **to the reader**.
- 2–3 paragraphs, each with a topic sentence (from B1).
- A **lively but not chatty** tone, and an ending that leaves the reader with a question, a tip or a challenge.

id.text:
Baca tulisanmu sekali lagi sebelum kamu mengunggahnya.
**Review** (140–190 kata):
- Judul dan **hook**; deskripsi singkat dengan **present simple**, **tanpa spoiler**.
- Minimal dua **kelebihan** dan satu **kekurangan**, masing-masing dengan **contoh spesifik**, dan kata penilaian, bukan *good / nice / bad*.
- **Adil**: *Although* + kekurangannya, lalu pendapat utamamu.
- **Rekomendasi** dan **cocok untuk siapa**: *I'd recommend + -ing / that you + kata kerja*, *I'd highly recommend it to …*, *It's well worth a try if …*. Bukan *recommend you to*.
**Artikel** (140–190 kata):
- **Judul** berupa pertanyaan, angka atau pun.
- **Pembuka** berupa pertanyaan, fakta yang mengejutkan atau anekdot, dan kamu bicara **kepada pembaca**.
- 2–3 paragraf, masing-masing dengan topic sentence (dari B1).
- Nada yang **hidup tapi tidak terlalu santai**, dan penutup yang meninggalkan pertanyaan, tips atau tantangan untuk pembaca.

blocks.text: Write your hook and your title **last**. When you've finished the text, you know what's most interesting about it, and that's what goes at the top.

id.text: Tulis hook dan judulmu **terakhir**. Setelah tulisanmu selesai, kamu tahu bagian mana yang paling menarik, dan itulah yang ditaruh paling atas.

id.intro: Selamat datang lagi! Di B1 kamu sudah menulis review pendek dengan rekomendasi. Sekarang kamu akan menulis seperti reviewer dan blogger sungguhan: review serial, aplikasi atau kafe yang menilai dengan adil dan menyebut dengan jelas siapa yang sebaiknya mencobanya, dan artikel dengan judul dan kalimat pertama yang membuat orang ingin terus membaca. Pemanasan: ingat-ingat serial terakhir yang tidak bisa berhenti kamu tonton, atau aplikasi yang tidak bisa kamu tinggalkan.

Apa yang salah dengan 'I recommend you to watch it'?
Bisa beri aku kata-kata lain seperti gripping dan user-friendly?

assessment.rva-2: Lengkapi review Sari tentang serial Netflix dengan SATU kata sifat bahasa Inggris yang artinya 'seru sekali sampai tidak bisa berhenti menonton': I started episode 1 at nine in the evening and only stopped at three in the morning. The story is absolutely ___ .
assessment.rva-3: Pendapat Rina tentang sebuah kafe di Bandung secara keseluruhan positif. Gabungkan dua kalimatnya menjadi satu kalimat bahasa Inggris yang diawali dengan Although: The café is overpriced. The view of the city is stunning.

Judul mana yang akan membuat paling banyak orang ingin membacanya? Tulis A, B atau C. A: E-Wallets B: Can You Survive a Week Without Cash? assessment.rva-5: Dimas sedang menulis artikel untuk majalah kampusnya tentang kafe-kafe terbaik di Bandung untuk belajar. Pembuka mana yang paling bagus? Tulis A, B atau C. A: Hello guys!! Welcome back to my article hehe. Today I want to share about cafés for studying. B: In this article, I will discuss the advantages and disadvantages of studying in cafés in Bandung.
